Answer: D
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates complete opacification of the left hemithorax with significant ipsilateral mediastinal shift (trachea and heart displaced to the left), which is the hallmark radiographic sign distinguishing pulmonary aplasia/agenesis from space-occupying lesions like massive effusion; while atelectasis also causes ipsilateral shift, the total absence of lung tissue in aplasia makes this displacement a primary defining feature compared to the other options which are either non-specific or not visible on plain film. *(guided by t000002)*
